Định luật khí lý tưởng: $n = \\frac{PV}{RT} = \\frac{80\\,\\mathrm{atm}\\times 12\\,\\mathrm{L}}{0.0821\\,\\mathrm{L\\,atm\\,mol^{-1}\\,K^{-1}}\\times 290\\,\\mathrm{K}} \\approx 40.4\\,\\mathrm{mol}$. Item 0: short_answer. Compute work done by gas at constant pressure moving piston from 30 cm to 35 cm. Cylinder diameter 20 cm => radius 10 cm = 0.1 m. Area A = π r^2 = π *0.01 = 0.01π m^2. Pressure = 102 kPa = 102,000 Pa. Work = P * ΔV (since constant pressure, work done by gas = P * (V_final - V_initial)). ΔV = A * Δh where Δh = (35-30) cm = 5 cm = 0.05 m. So ΔV = 0.01π * 0.05 = 0.0005π m^3. Compute: π≈3.1416 => ΔV≈0.0005*3.1416=0.0015708 m^3. Work = 102,000 * 0.0015708 ≈ 160.2216 J. Positive work done by gas (expansion). The source options include -0.16 J, -160 J, 0.16 J, 160 J. So correct answer is 160 J (positive). Need short answer numeric with unit J. Probably 1.6×10^2 J. Provide 160 J.

Total mass of seat+ cylinder = 6 kg. Student mass = 24 kg. So total weight = (6+24) * g = 30 kg *10 = 300 N.

When seated, the system is in equilibrium with piston displaced down 12 cm (0.12 m). The gas exerts upward force = (p_atm + p_gauge) * A. The downward forces are weight (300 N) plus atmospheric pressure acting on piston? Actually atmospheric pressure acts on both sides of piston? The piston is inside cylinder, top side is atmospheric? Usually gauge pressure is pressure above atmospheric inside cylinder. The piston experiences external atmospheric pressure on top (outside cylinder) pushing down, and internal pressure (p0 + p_gauge) pushing up on piston area. The net upward force = (p0 + p_gauge) * A - p0 * A = p_gauge * A. Wait if top side is open to atmosphere, then atmospheric pressure acts on top of piston, but internal pressure also includes atmospheric. So net upward force due to gas = p_gauge * A. That must balance weight (since static). So p_gauge = weight / A.

Compute weight = 300 N. Area = 3.0e-3 m^2. So p_gauge = 300 / 0.003 = 100,000 Pa = 1.0e5 Pa.

Options: 8.0×10^4 Pa, 1.5×10^5 Pa, 1.0×10^5 Pa, 5.0×10^4 Pa. So correct is 1.0×10^5 Pa (third option, index 2 zero-based). Provide.

Now item 2: short_answer. Compute mass of nitrogen.

Given: V = 12 L = 0.012 m^3. Pressure = 80 atm. Temperature = 17°C = 290 K (since 273+17 = 290 K). Molar mass M = 28 g/mol = 0.028 kg/mol.

Use ideal gas: PV = nRT. Need R in SI: 0.082057 L·atm·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹? But easier: Use R = 0.082057 L·atm/(mol·K). Use V in L, P in atm, T in K. Then n = PV/(R T). Compute: P=80 atm, V=12 L, T=290 K. n = (80*12)/(0.082057*290). Compute numerator 960. Denominator 0.082057*290 = 23.79553. n = 960 / 23.7955 ≈ 40.36 mol.

Mass = n * M = 40.36 mol * 28 g/mol = 1130.1 g = 1.13 kg.
